## Natural history notes

A medium-sized bark mantis characterized by a flattened gray to brown body, mottled bark-like camouflage, and a broad triangular head with large eyes. In Florida, the Grizzled Mantis is found on tree trunks, branches, fences, and woody vegetation in hammocks, pine flatwoods, scrub, parks, gardens, and forest edges. It is an ambush predator, remaining motionless against bark until insects or other small arthropods come within reach, then seizing them with its spiny raptorial forelegs.
